item.title: Learning to Love the Liberal Arts
item.description: At Hillsdale College, on average, 31 percent of the incoming freshman class comes from public school backgrounds. Sometimes, there’s an academic adjustment, but those students are not any less qualified to partake in Hillsdale’s liberal arts education. Quinn Delamater, ’26, explains.

item.title: Don’t Neglect the Gift: Legacy in the Roberts Sisters’ Strides
item.description: Not everyone considers running a gift, but for the Roberts family, it is the gift that keeps on giving. Anna, ’26, Megan, ’27, Caroline, ’29, are carrying the family legacy forward, running their own races at their own paces for the Chargers.

item.title: Why WHIP? Do It For the Challenge
item.description: I can confidently say my semester on WHIP was one of the best I’ve ever had at Hillsdale College. This is part three of a three-part series explaining why you should spend a semester on WHIP during your time at Hillsdale College.

item.title: Find Your Strength: Emma Ruhlman’s Breakout Basketball Season
item.description: From a freshman on the bench to a starting senior, Emma Ruhlman has truly blossomed during her years as a Charger. During her junior year, she had found her strength, earning a spot in the starting lineup and helping the Chargers to their best season in 16 years.

item.title: Leading at Home, Learning on Campus: Parenting in Grad School
item.description: Some undergrad Hillsdale students look to begin graduate school after they leave campus. But for many of Hillsdale’s graduate students, the transition was not immediate. A handful of residential grad students have not only begun careers, but many also started raising children. Here's how they juggle it all.

item.title: Why WHIP? Do It for the People
item.description: Grace Canlas, '27, can confidently say her semester on the Washington-Hillsdale Internship Program (WHIP) was one of the best she has ever had at Hillsdale College. This is part one of a three-part series explaining why you should spend a semester on WHIP during your time at Hillsdale College.

item.title: The Hillsdale RA Difference
item.description: Hillsdale Resident Assistants aren’t student security–they’re the heart of dorm culture and community across campus. Being a Resident Assistant at Hillsdale bonds you to your RA team and residents in unforgettable ways.

item.title: The Hard Things: Muellers Carve Out Community Life in Colorado
item.description: “Family, church, and local community” was the mantra of longtime (and now retired) Hillsdale College history professor John Willson. Paul and Kathryn Williams Mueller, ’09, ’09, are living that reality in the remote mining town of Leadville, Colorado, nestled in the Rocky Mountains.

item.title: Four Years and Counting
item.description: Four years. A lot can happen during that time. It certainly has for Doug Goodnough, '90. Heading into Year 5 of his role at the College, he's excited to see the growing Alumni Office in action.

item.title: Hometown Hillsdale: Colleen Vogt, ’90
item.description: Colleen Colosimo Vogt knew from a young age that she wanted to work in a school setting. Education, learning, and athletics were her passions, and they ultimately led her to Hillsdale College. Colleen leads Will Carleton Academy in Hillsdale and has been at the helm from the very beginning.

item.title: Libraries, Towers, and Unforgettable Hours: The Oxford Study-Abroad Experience
item.description: Last summer, students Megan and Faith spent six weeks at the University of Oxford through the Oxford Study Abroad Programme. Megan studied comparative economics while Faith studied British poetry.

item.title: Totalitarian Technology: Dr. Diener Teaches a Course on Technology and Education
item.description: Associate Professor of Education David Diener is offering a course that tackles the questions of how technology relates to education and human flourishing. His students are considering the nature of technology and will also partake in a series of “technology fasts” to reflect on technology’s role in daily life.

item.title: Why WHIP? Do It For the Adventure
item.description: I can confidently say my semester on WHIP was one of the best I’ve ever had at Hillsdale College. This is part two of a three-part series explaining why you should spend a semester on WHIP during your time at Hillsdale College.

item.title: A Classical Curtain Call
item.description: A liberal arts college doesn’t feel complete without a strong theatre department. Theatre at Hillsdale College certainly doesn’t disappoint on or behind the stage. Stepping behind the curtain allowed Adam Robbins, '27, to understand how the Department has cultivated a robust community among a variety of students studying many different things, who bond over a general love of theatre.

item.title: Hillsdale Made Me a Teacher (And Brought Me Back)
item.description: As an undergrad, Nolan Ryan, ’20, decided to pursue a career in education thanks to inspiration from Hillsdale’s professors. With several years of teaching under his belt, he returned to campus as a grad student to deepen his experience and understanding of classical education.
